P. Ravinder Reddy, Secbad vs Santhosh And Another on 15
February, 2024
Author: P. Sam Koshy

Bench: P.Sam Koshy, N.Tukaramji
 Honourable Sri Justice P. Sam Koshy
 And
 Honourable Sri Justice N. Tukaramji
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2702 Of 2011
 And
 M.A.C.M.A. No.2836 Of 2011
Common Judgment

:
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice N. Tukaramji) M.A.C.M.A.No.2702 of 2011 is filed by the respondent No.2/insurer contesting the liability and quantum of compensation; whereas the M.A.C.M.A.No.2836 of 2011 is filed by the petitioner seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded in the decree and order dated 06.06.2011 in O.P.No.90 of 2008 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional Chief Judge- cum City Civil Court, at Secunderabad.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional Chief Judge- cum City Civil Court, at Secunderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. We have heard Mr. Somanchi Venkateshwarlu, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr.
Sudershan S. Reddy, learned counsel for the respondent No.2/insurer.
3. For convenience, the appellants are hereinafter referred to as per their array before the tribunal.
2 Pskj&ntrj Macma_2702_2011&macma_2836_2011 4.

The case of the petitioner is that, on 11.03.2008 while he was travelling in the car bearing registration No.KA-03-B-2980 to Gulbarga, at Shapur one lorry bearing registration No. KA 32 8452 driven in rash and negligent manner dashed the car and caused severe injuries on his head,
ribs, upper and lower limbs.
Thereupon, claiming medical expenditure, disability and other damages filed petition seeking compensation of Rs.50 lakhs.
5. In inquiry, the petitioner got himself examined as the PW-1.

Further examined his treating doctors as the PW-2 and PW-4, the Billing Manager of Yashoda Hospitals as the PW-3, the Manager of Vision Academy as the PW-5, the doctor who issued disability certificate as the PW-6 and got marked Exs:A-1 to A-27.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2/insurer got examined its employee as RW-1 and marked Exs:B-1 to B-3.
6.

The Tribunal on considering the materials awarded compensation of Rs.28,19,780/- with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of the petition till realization against the insured and the insurer of P. sentences.text: In appeal, learned counsel for the petitioner contested that the tribunal had erred in properly appreciating the disability suffered by the petitioner, particularly the evidence of the doctor/PW-4 that the petitioner is suffering with visual field deficit of both the eyes and difficulty in reading and visualizing objects, which are essential for an occupation of lecturer, as such the occupational disability should have been rated at 100%.
Further the tribunal had taken the net income than gross income setforth in Form No.16 in assessment of compensation.
That apart, a meager amount was granted towards pain and suffering and amenities.
The future medical necessities are not accounted in compensation.
Thus prayed for enhancement of the awarded amount.

8. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2/insurer would submit that the tribunal had failed to consider that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving licence and the effort of the respondent No.2/insurer to reach the insured/respondent No.1 under notice/Ex.B-2 remained futile.

However, considering the charge under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'the Act') against the driver of the offending 4 Pskj&ntrj Macma_2702_2011&macma_2836_2011 vehicle in the charge sheet /Ex.A-2, the tribunal should have absolved the liability of the respondent No.2/insurer for violation of policy condition.

Further contended that though the tribunal had noted the physical disability at 45%, calculated the loss of earnings at the same proportion by ignoring the principle that in assessment of compensation the effect of permanent disability on the earning capacity shall only be considered.
That apart, the petitioner got examined unrelated person to prove the medical bills/A-17 as such allowing the bills in compensation is improper.
Hence prayed for considering these aspects and to determine the compensation.

9. In the contra pleas, the aspects arise for determination are:
(a) Whether the respondent No.2/insurer has established violation of the policy condition i.e. the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence at relevant time, to absolve its liability?
(b) Whether the awarded compensation to the petitioner is just and proper?
5 Pskj&ntrj Macma_2702_2011&macma_2836_2011
10 . In regard to the liability, the respondent No.2/insurer contended that as the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving licence, it shall be exonerated.
To prove this aspect except placing Ex.B-2 letter to the insured, no other evidence has been brought on record.
Further in the charge sheet/Ex.A-2 the driver of the offending vehicle was charged under Section 187 of the Act which deals with the punishment for the offences relating to accident.
Notably, Section 181 of the Act deals with driving of vehicle without necessary driving licence and this section was not part of the charge sheet.
Therefore, to support the plea disputing the driving licence, no document or material is on record at least to adverse inference.

For the failure of respondent No.2/insurer in P. Ravinder Reddy, Secbad vs Santhosh And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67032958/
2 discharging onus, this contention fails.

sentences.text: 11. The treating doctor/PW-2 deposed about the injuries/fractures suffered and the treatment undergone by the petitioner.
The Doctor categorically stated that the petitioner would continue to suffer stiffness, disability in walking and squatting.
6 Pskj&ntrj Macma_2702_2011&macma_2836_2011 12.
The Ophthalmologist/PW-4 testified that the petitioner is suffering with visual field deficit in both the eyes and he would face difficulty in reading and visualizing the objects.
The Orthopaedic Surgeon/PW-6 who was Member of the Medical Board issued the disability certificate/Ex.A-20 stated that the physical disability of the petitioner is partial in nature at 45%.
Pertinently, the treating doctor/PW-2 stated that the petitioner would be able to work as lecturer.

Having regard to the medical evidence as to the physical disability and the nature of occupation, we are of the considered opinion that the extent of physical disability rated by the doctors would partially have an effect in performing the occupational activities.
In this view, the tribunal rated disability is found justified and thus affirmed.

13. In regard to the earnings of the petitioner, the Form 16 is showing gross income at Rs.3,32,068/-
and deduction of income tax at Rs.16,356/-.
It is settled position that the actual income has to be arrived by deducting the tax amount payable from the gross income.
Accordingly the annual income of the petitioner shall be taken at Rs.3,15,712/-.

In addition as per the authority of Pappu Deo 7 Pskj&ntrj Macma_2702_2011&macma_2836_2011 Yadav v. V. Naresh Kumar and others 1 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi and others2, for the age and nature of employment of the petitioner, 40% of the income has to be added towards future prospects which makes the annual income at Rs.4,43,397/- and as the petitioner is suffering occupational disability at 45% the loss of annual income earnings would be Rs.1,99,529/-.

sentences.text: The petitioner is entitled to this amount for the loss of earnings due to disability.
14. The respondent No.2/insurer disputed proof of Ex.A-17/medical bills.
The petitioner as PW-1 deposed about the expenditure incurred for medication under the bills/Ex.A-17 and Ex.A-18 as prescribed by the doctors.

Neither the prescriptions nor the administration of medicine shown in the bills during the treatment are disputed either in the cross examination of PW-1 or 1 2020 SCC O n l i n e S C 7 5 2 2 ( 2 0 1 7 ) 1 6 S C C 8 6 0 3 2 0 0 9 A C J 1 2 9 8 8 P s k j & n t r j Macma_2702_2011&macma_2836_2011 the treating doctor/PW-2.
In this position and in absence of any other material to discredit, the amount of Rs.8,40,000/- in Ex:A-17 and Ex.A-18 merits reimbursement.

15. Further having regard to the injuries suffered and the evidence of doctor that the petitioner will continue to have the disability and probable medical necessities, we are inclined to grant Rs.1,00,000/- towards future medical necessities.

sentences.text: Having regard to the multiple fractures, surgeries and the treatment undergone and plausible future sufferings, we deem it appropriate to grant Rs.2,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings, in the place of amounts granted for injuries and the pain and sufferings by the tribunal.
Thus in all, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.43,32,458/-.
The rate of interest and the other terms imposed by the tribunal shall remain the same.

17. Accordingly the awarded compensation is modified to Rs.43,32,458/- (Rupees forty three lakhs thirty two thousand four hundred and fifty eight only) with interest at 7.5% per annum from the d a t e o f p e t i t i o n t i l l r e a l i s a t i o n . T h e r e s p o n d e n t N o .

2 / i n s u e r 9 P s k j & n t r j Macma_2702_2011&macma_2836_2011 shall deposit the awarded compensation by setting of the amounts already paid/deposited, within 4 (four) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
18. Resultantly, the M.A.C.M.A.No.2702 of 2011 filed by the respondent No.2/insurer is dismissed without costs.
The M.A.C.M.A.No.2836 of 2011 filed by the petitioner is partly allowed with proportionate costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions if any, stand closed.

13. In regard to the earnings of the petitioner, the Form 16 is showing gross income at Rs.3,32,068/-

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly the annual income of the petitioner shall be taken at Rs.3,15,712/-.
If this amount is multiplied with appropriate multiplier to the age of the petitioner as per Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another3 i.e. 16, the amount would come to Rs.31,92,458/-.
The petitioner is entitled to this amount for the loss of earnings due to disability.
14. The respondent No.2/insurer disputed proof of Ex.A-17/medical bills.
The petitioner as PW-1 deposed about the expenditure incurred for medication under the bills/Ex.A-17 and Ex.A-18 as prescribed by the doctors.
In this position and in absence of any other material to discredit, the amount of Rs.8,40,000/- in Ex:A-17 and Ex.A-18 merits reimbursement.
15. Further having regard to the injuries suffered and the evidence of doctor that the petitioner will continue to have the disability and probable medical necessities, we are inclined to grant Rs.1,00,000/- towards future medical necessities.
Having regard to the multiple fractures, surgeries and the treatment undergone and plausible future sufferings, we deem it appropriate to grant Rs.2,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings, in the place of amounts granted for injuries and the pain and sufferings by the tribunal.
Thus in all, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.43,32,458/-.
The rate of interest and the other terms imposed by the tribunal shall remain the same.
17. Accordingly the awarded compensation is modified to Rs.43,32,458/- (Rupees forty three lakhs thirty two thousand four hundred and fifty eight only) with interest at 7.5% per annum from the d a t e o f p e t i t i o n t i l l r e a l i s a t i o n . T h e r e s p o n d e n t N o .
